**7.0 COMMUNICATION & INCIDENT PROTOCOLS**

**7.1 Command Structure (Show Days)**

The following lines of communication apply during the 2025 festival period (2025-03-14 to
2025-03-19, inclusive of load-in/load-out):

- **Festival Director (Marcus Lim):** Overall authority. Final escalation point for all
  incidents, budget overruns, and media-related matters.
- **Ops Control Room (OCR):** Single point of contact for all radio traffic. Located at the
  Production Office, Bayfront Pavilion. Ext. 2104. Staffed 24/7 from 2025-03-13 06:00 to
  2025-03-20 18:00.
- **Dept Heads:** Report directly to OCR. Each dept head carries one primary radio (Channel 1)
  and one backup (Channel 5).
- **Security Command:** Reports to OCR for crowd management issues; liaises directly with
  Singapore Police Force (SPF) liaison officer on-site for any arrests or medical emergencies.

**7.2 Radio Channels**

| Channel | Purpose | Notes |
|---------|---------|-------|
| 1 | Ops Control (primary) | All dept heads; OCR logs all traffic |
| 2 | Security / Crowd Mgmt | Security team, medical, SPF liaison |
| 3 | Stage / Production | Stage manager, artist liaison, AV |
| 4 | Logistics / Crew | Load-in/out, transport, catering |
| 5 | Backup / Admin | Only if Channel 1 fails; OCR to announce switch |

**7.3 Incident Reporting Flow**

1. **Initial report** to OCR via radio (Channel 1) or phone (ext. 2104).
2. OCR logs the incident in the Incident Log (shared drive: BBF-2025-INC) with time, location,
   and nature.
3. OCR assigns a severity level (see 7.4) and notifies the relevant dept head.
4. For Severity 2 and above, OCR notifies the Festival Director immediately.
5. **Written follow-up** within 2 hours: dept head submits a short incident report to OCR using
   the template in Appendix C. The report must include what happened, actions taken, and any
   follow-up required.
6. OCR closes the incident only after the dept head confirms resolution. All logs are retained
   for post-event review.

**7.4 Severity Levels**

- **Severity 1 (Minor):** No impact to public or show. Example: minor equipment fault with
  immediate fix. No escalation beyond dept head.
- **Severity 2 (Moderate):** Potential impact to a single area or act. Example: artist delay
  of 15 min, small crowd surge. Escalate to Festival Director; consider public announcement.
- **Severity 3 (Major):** Show stoppage, safety incident, or media attention. Example: power
  failure, injury requiring hospitalisation, evacuation. Festival Director takes lead; SPF and
  SCDF notified as needed.

Note: For any Severity 3 incident, the Festival Director or delegate is the only person
authorised to speak to media. All other staff must direct media queries to the Press Office.

**7.5 Weather Contingency**

The 2025 edition falls within the traditional afternoon thunderstorm season. The following
triggers apply:

- **Lightning within 10 km:** Stop outdoor stage activity immediately. Seek shelter. Resume
  only after 30 minutes with no lightning detected.
- **Heavy rain (forecast or actual):** OCR to issue a "Rain Alert" via radio. Stage manager
  decides whether to pause or continue based on stage cover and artist safety.
- **Wind above 60 km/h:** Secure all loose structures. Outdoor stages to be evacuated if wind

The weather monitoring service (WeatherWatch SG) provides a dedicated feed to OCR. The

Measurement shall be taken at the nearest residential façade or at a distance of
25 metres from the sound source boundary, whichever is more restrictive. For venues
with no residential receptors within 200 metres, the measurement point shall be at the
venue boundary line.

4. MEASUREMENT PROCEDURES
4.1 Approved Sound Level Meters
Only Class 1 or Class 2 sound level meters (SLMs) conforming to IEC 61672-1 shall be
used for compliance measurement. The SLM must have a valid calibration certificate
issued within the past 12 months. Calibration certificates shall be kept on file by the
Production Office and made available to NEA officers upon request.

4.2 Measurement Frequency
- Continuous logging: For events lasting more than 4 hours, a real-time logging SLM
  shall be set up at the primary measurement point, recording data at 1-minute
  intervals.
- Spot checks: For events lasting less than 4 hours, spot checks shall be conducted
  every 30 minutes, with each check lasting at least 5 minutes.
- Post-event review: Logged data shall be reviewed within 24 hours of event
  completion by the Head of Operations or designate.

4.3 Weather Adjustments
Measurements shall be suspended during periods of heavy rain (rainfall rate exceeding
10 mm per hour) or when wind speed exceeds 15 knots, as these conditions affect
microphone response. If measurements are suspended for more than 30 minutes, the
event shall be deemed to have a measurement gap, and the Production Manager shall
document the reason and estimated sound levels during the gap.

4.4 Calibration Checks
Field calibration shall be performed before the first measurement and after the last
measurement of each event day. A calibration deviation of more than 0.5 dB shall
invalidate all measurements taken between the two calibration points.

5. CURFEW SCHEDULE
The following curfew hours apply to all outdoor productions. These hours are
stricter than the NEA’s standard curfew in certain zones and are adopted as a
community relations measure.

| Venue Type | Weekdays (Mon–Thu) | Fridays | Saturdays | Sundays & PH |
|------------|--------------------|---------|-----------|----------------|
| Park/Open Field | 22:00 | 23:00 | 23:30 | 22:30 |
| Waterfront | 22:30 | 23:30 | 00:00 | 23:00 |
| Indoor w/ residential adjac. | 23:00 | 23:30 | 00:00 | 23:00 |

The Noise Control Policy sets max_decibel_limit at 90 dB. Record status: current.

Note: Curfew refers to the time by which all amplified sound must cease. Sound
checks and rehearsals must be completed at least 30 minutes before the curfew time.

6. FREQUENCY WEIGHTING AND AVERAGING
All measurements shall use A-weighting (dBA) unless otherwise specified by the
NEA or by the venue’s licence conditions. The Leq over 15 minutes shall be the
primary metric for compliance. In addition, the Lpeak (peak sound pressure level)
shall not exceed 120 dBA at any time, regardless of duration.

For events with multiple sound sources (e.g., multiple stages), each stage shall be
measured independently, and the combined effect shall be assessed by the Production
Manager. If the combined Leq is expected to exceed 90 dB, the sound engineers for
each stage shall coordinate to reduce output.

7. ROLES AND RESPONSIBILITIES
7.1 Production Manager
- Overall responsibility for compliance with this policy.
- Appoints a designated Noise Monitor for each event.
- Reviews logged data and signs off on the post-event noise report.

7.2 Noise Monitor
- Operates the SLM and records measurements.
- Reports any exceedance immediately to the Production Manager and the stage
  sound engineer.
- Maintains the measurement log in the format specified in Appendix A.

7.3 Sound Engineer (Head of Sound)
- Ensures system configuration (speaker placement, EQ, limiting) is set to avoid
  exceedances.
- Adjusts levels upon instruction from the Noise Monitor.
- Provides technical explanation for any exceedance.

8. CURFEW SCHEDULE AND AMPLIFIED SOUND CEASURE

8.1 General Curfew Time

The Noise Control Policy curfew_time is 22:30. Record status: current. This is the standard curfew time for all events under this policy, unless a later time is approved under the conditions in Section 8.3 below. Curfew time means the time by which all amplified sound must cease, including sound checks, rehearsals, and any audio output from stage monitors, PA systems, or broadcast speakers. This applies to both indoor and outdoor venues within the event site, including back-of-house areas where amplified sound may be audible to the public or nearby residential premises.

All event schedules shall be planned such that the final musical performance or programme item ends no later than 15 minutes before the curfew time. This buffer allows for encores, on-stage announcements, and the orderly fade-out of sound. The curfew time is not the same as the venue's operational closing time; the venue may remain open for audience egress, food and beverage sales, and non-amplified activities, subject to the venue's own licence conditions.

8.2 Curfew by Venue Type and Day

The following table sets out the curfew times applicable to different venue types. These are the curfew times, meaning amplified sound must cease by the stated time. Where the venue type is not listed, the curfew time shall be 22:30 unless otherwise approved.

Note: For Sundays and public holidays, the curfew time reverts to 22:30 for park/open field venues. This is to account for the following day being a working day for most residents.

8.3 Extensions and Exceptions

Requests for a later curfew time may be submitted to the Production Manager in writing at least 14 days before the event. The following criteria shall be considered:

- Distance to nearest residential premises (minimum 150 m for a 30-minute extension; minimum 300 m for a 60-minute extension)
- Historical noise complaint records for the venue
- Whether the event is a national or community event with a public interest justification
- Weather conditions (e.g., a delayed start due to an afternoon thunderstorm may justify a later end time, but not a later curfew)

Approved extensions shall be recorded in the event's Noise Management Plan and communicated to the Noise Monitor and sound engineers. Extensions are not automatically granted and must be confirmed in writing by the Production Manager.

8.4 Sound Checks and Rehearsals

Sound checks and rehearsals are subject to the same curfew time as the main event. All sound checks must be completed at least 30 minutes before the curfew time. This means that if the curfew is 22:30, all sound checks must be completed by 22:00.

During sound checks, the Noise Monitor shall take preliminary measurements and note any potential exceedance of the 90 dB limit. If the sound check indicates that the main performance is likely to exceed the limit, the Sound Engineer shall adjust the system configuration before the performance begins. No sound check may be conducted after the curfew time, even if the main event has not yet started.

9. ENFORCEMENT AND MONITORING PROCEDURES

9.1 Noise Monitor Duties During Event

The Noise Monitor shall:

- Take measurements at 15-minute intervals throughout the event, starting at least 30 minutes before the first performance and continuing until 15 minutes after the curfew time.
- Record the Leq, Lpeak, and the time of each measurement in the log sheet (Appendix A).
- Note the location of each measurement and any relevant conditions (e.g., wind direction, crowd noise, nearby construction).
- Immediately report any reading that exceeds 90 dB (Leq, 15-min) or 120 dBA (Lpeak) to the Production Manager and the stage Sound Engineer.

**1. PURPOSE**

This policy establishes the framework for managing noise emissions from all Lumina Events activities, including but not limited to concerts, festivals, corporate functions, and community events held at venues operated or managed by Lumina Events Pte Ltd. The purpose is to ensure compliance with the National Environment Agency (NEA) regulations, to minimise disturbance to surrounding residents and businesses, and to maintain good community relations.

This policy applies to all Lumina Events staff, contractors, sub-contractors, volunteers, and artists performing at Lumina Events venues or events. It also applies to external parties who hire Lumina Events venues for their own events, and such parties shall be made aware of this policy as part of the venue hire agreement.

**2. DEFINITIONS**

For the purposes of this policy, the following terms shall have the meanings described below:

- **Ambient Noise:** The background noise level at a given location, measured in the absence of the event noise. This is typically measured during a quiet period, such as early afternoon, and is used as a baseline for assessing the impact of event noise.
- **Curfew Time:** The time by which all amplified sound, including sound checks and rehearsals, must cease. The standard curfew time is 22:30 hours, unless a written extension has been approved under Section 8.3.
- **Decibel (dB):** A unit of measurement for sound intensity. Unless otherwise specified, all decibel limits in this policy refer to A-weighted decibels (dBA) for Lpeak and Leq,15min measurements.
- **Intermittent Event:** An event or portion of an event that produces sound at irregular intervals, with periods of relative quiet between performances or announcements. Examples include multi-stage festivals where stages alternate, or events with scheduled breaks.
- **Leq,15min:** The equivalent continuous sound level measured over a 15-minute period. This is the primary metric used for assessing compliance with the 90 dB limit.
- **Lpeak:** The peak sound pressure level, measured instantaneously. This is used to assess the risk of hearing damage and sudden loud noises.
- **Noise Monitor:** A trained individual appointed by the Production Manager to carry out sound level measurements and report on compliance. The Noise Monitor shall be independent of the sound system provider.
- **Noise Management Plan (NMP):** A document prepared for each event, detailing the predicted sound levels, mitigation measures, monitoring arrangements, and contingency plans. The NMP shall be submitted to the relevant authorities as required.
- **Sound Engineer:** The individual responsible for the operation of the sound system during the event, including system configuration, mixing, and ensuring compliance with the sound level limits.
- **Venue Boundary:** The physical boundary of the event site, as indicated on the site plan attached to the NMP. For venues without a defined boundary, the boundary shall be the perimeter of the area under Lumina Events' control.

This document consolidates the crowd management arrangements for Lumina Events Pte Ltd outdoor and mixed-venue events held within Singapore. 2.0 Venue Capacity Determination

2.1 General Principle

The maximum capacity for any event site is determined by the lesser of the physical site capacity, the approved capacity under the Fire Safety (Events Venues) Order, and the operational capacity recommended by the Safety & Security Consultant. The maximum capacity figure is fixed for the current calendar year and is not adjusted on a per-event basis unless a formal variation is approved by the relevant authorities.

The Crowd Management Plan max_capacity is 50000 people. Record status: current. This figure is current for the 2025 edition and applies to the main festival grounds at Bayfront Green, including the open field area, the promenade extensions, and the designated viewing zones. The figure excludes performers, crew, vendors, and accredited media personnel, who are accounted for separately under the staffing and production headcount.

2.2 Capacity Calculation Basis

The site is divided into zones for the purpose of capacity calculation and crowd density monitoring. Each zone has its own holding capacity, which when summed, equals the overall maximum capacity. The zoning reflects the physical layout, the location of entry and exit points, and the internal circulation routes.

The transit buffer is not intended for prolonged occupation; it exists to absorb the surge of people entering or exiting during peak periods. If the transit buffer becomes congested for more than 10 minutes, entry is paused at the affected gates.

2.3 Density Monitoring

Zone density is monitored using a combination of manual headcounts at the gates, CCTV analytics at key pinch points, and steward patrols with handheld counters. The density standard for each zone is set out in Table 2.1 above. The following thresholds trigger action:

- 80% of zone holding capacity: Stewards at the zone entry points begin to hold back incoming attendees, and the zone controller is notified.

Density is monitored centrally at the Crowd Safety Cell (CSC), located in the North Command Post (NCP). The CSC operates from 10:00 to 24:00 on event days, with a skeleton team from 08:00 (for load-in checks). Key monitoring tools:

- **CCTV Analytics:** 42 cameras across 11 zones, with automated people-counting software. Calibration is checked each morning against manual counts at 3 fixed reference points.
- **Handheld Counters:** Stewards at zone entry/exit points conduct 10-minute manual counts during peak periods (17:00–21:00).

All density readings are logged in the CSC Daily Log (Form CSC-7). The log is reviewed at the end of each event day by the Event Director and the Safety & Security Lead.

The following protocols are activated based on the density levels in Table 4.1. These are in addition to the zone-specific capacity actions in Section 2.3.

- Zone Controllers confirm receipt and identify the affected zone(s).
- Gate stewards begin holding entry at the affected zone(s) for 30-second intervals.
- Additional stewards are dispatched from the reserve pool (minimum 4 per affected zone).
- The Event Director is informed verbally, but no written report is required unless the level persists for > 30 minutes.

**Protocol 2 – Zone Hold (≥ 3.2 persons/sqm)**

**Protocol 3 – Zone Closure (≥ 3.6 persons/sqm)**

- Zone entry is closed to all new attendees.
- PA and digital signage broadcast re-routing messages (pre-recorded message "Route B" or "Route C", depending on the zone).
- Exit gates are widened where possible (barriers moved by stewards).
- The Event Director is formally notified via radio and a written SMS alert.
- SCDF Liaison (Kelvin Chua) is informed if the closure lasts > 15 minutes.

**Protocol 4 – Full Stop (≥ 4.0 persons/sqm)**

**Post-Incident Requirements:**

**Radio Etiquette:**

- All radio transmissions shall begin with the call sign of the recipient followed by the call sign of the sender. Example: "ZC-East, this is CSC, over."
- Use plain English. Avoid jargon or slang. Do not use "lah" or other Singlish particles on the radio channel, as these can cause confusion during high-stress situations.
- Acknowledge all instructions with "Copy" or "Received." If an instruction is unclear, respond with "Say again" or "Blur, please repeat."

**7.0 COMMUNICATION & INCIDENT PROTOCOLS**

**7.1 Command Structure (Show Days)**

The following lines of communication apply during the 2025 festival period (2025-03-14 to
2025-03-19, inclusive of load-in/load-out):

- **Festival Director (Marcus Lim):** Overall authority. Final escalation point for all
  incidents, budget overruns, and media-related matters.
- **Ops Control Room (OCR):** Single point of contact for all radio traffic. Located at the
  Production Office, Bayfront Pavilion. Ext. 2104. Staffed 24/7 from 2025-03-13 06:00 to
  2025-03-20 18:00.
- **Dept Heads:** Report directly to OCR. Each dept head carries one primary radio (Channel 1)
  and one backup (Channel 5).
- **Security Command:** Reports to OCR for crowd management issues; liaises directly with
  Singapore Police Force (SPF) liaison officer on-site for any arrests or medical emergencies.

**7.2 Radio Channels**

| Channel | Purpose | Notes |
|---------|---------|-------|
| 1 | Ops Control (primary) | All dept heads; OCR logs all traffic |
| 2 | Security / Crowd Mgmt | Security team, medical, SPF liaison |
| 3 | Stage / Production | Stage manager, artist liaison, AV |
| 4 | Logistics / Crew | Load-in/out, transport, catering |
| 5 | Backup / Admin | Only if Channel 1 fails; OCR to announce switch |

**7.3 Incident Reporting Flow**

1. **Initial report** to OCR via radio (Channel 1) or phone (ext. 2104).
2. OCR logs the incident in the Incident Log (shared drive: BBF-2025-INC) with time, location,
   and nature.
3. OCR assigns a severity level (see 7.4) and notifies the relevant dept head.
4. For Severity 2 and above, OCR notifies the Festival Director immediately.
5. **Written follow-up** within 2 hours: dept head submits a short incident report to OCR using
   the template in Appendix C. The report must include what happened, actions taken, and any
   follow-up required.
6. OCR closes the incident only after the dept head confirms resolution. All logs are retained
   for post-event review.

**7.4 Severity Levels**

- **Severity 1 (Minor):** No impact to public or show. Example: minor equipment fault with
  immediate fix. No escalation beyond dept head.
- **Severity 2 (Moderate):** Potential impact to a single area or act. Example: artist delay
  of 15 min, small crowd surge. Escalate to Festival Director; consider public announcement.
- **Severity 3 (Major):** Show stoppage, safety incident, or media attention. Example: power
  failure, injury requiring hospitalisation, evacuation. Festival Director takes lead; SPF and
  SCDF notified as needed.

Note: For any Severity 3 incident, the Festival Director or delegate is the only person
authorised to speak to media. All other staff must direct media queries to the Press Office.

**7.5 Weather Contingency**

The 2025 edition falls within the traditional afternoon thunderstorm season. The following
triggers apply:

- **Lightning within 10 km:** Stop outdoor stage activity immediately. Seek shelter. Resume
  only after 30 minutes with no lightning detected.
- **Heavy rain (forecast or actual):** OCR to issue a "Rain Alert" via radio. Stage manager
  decides whether to pause or continue based on stage cover and artist safety.
- **Wind above 60 km/h:** Secure all loose structures. Outdoor stages to be evacuated if wind
  exceeds 80 km/h.

The weather monitoring service (WeatherWatch SG) provides a dedicated feed to OCR. The
Festival Director has final authority on any weather-related postponement.

The following checklist applies to all festival editions. It is reviewed annually by the
Safety & Compliance Officer and updated as needed. This version is the current template; any
changes must be approved by the Festival Director.

documents.content:
Measurement shall be taken at the nearest residential façade or at a distance of
25 metres from the sound source boundary, whichever is more restrictive. For venues
with no residential receptors within 200 metres, the measurement point shall be at the
venue boundary line.

4. MEASUREMENT PROCEDURES
4.1 Approved Sound Level Meters
Only Class 1 or Class 2 sound level meters (SLMs) conforming to IEC 61672-1 shall be
used for compliance measurement. The SLM must have a valid calibration certificate
issued within the past 12 months. Calibration certificates shall be kept on file by the
Production Office and made available to NEA officers upon request.

4.2 Measurement Frequency
- Continuous logging: For events lasting more than 4 hours, a real-time logging SLM
  shall be set up at the primary measurement point, recording data at 1-minute
  intervals.
- Spot checks: For events lasting less than 4 hours, spot checks shall be conducted
  every 30 minutes, with each check lasting at least 5 minutes.
- Post-event review: Logged data shall be reviewed within 24 hours of event
  completion by the Head of Operations or designate.

4.3 Weather Adjustments
Measurements shall be suspended during periods of heavy rain (rainfall rate exceeding
10 mm per hour) or when wind speed exceeds 15 knots, as these conditions affect
microphone response. If measurements are suspended for more than 30 minutes, the
event shall be deemed to have a measurement gap, and the Production Manager shall
document the reason and estimated sound levels during the gap.

4.4 Calibration Checks
Field calibration shall be performed before the first measurement and after the last
measurement of each event day. A calibration deviation of more than 0.5 dB shall
invalidate all measurements taken between the two calibration points.

5. CURFEW SCHEDULE
The following curfew hours apply to all outdoor productions. These hours are
stricter than the NEA’s standard curfew in certain zones and are adopted as a
community relations measure.

| Venue Type | Weekdays (Mon–Thu) | Fridays | Saturdays | Sundays & PH |
|------------|--------------------|---------|-----------|----------------|
| Park/Open Field | 22:00 | 23:00 | 23:30 | 22:30 |
| Waterfront | 22:30 | 23:30 | 00:00 | 23:00 |
| Indoor w/ residential adjac. | 23:00 | 23:30 | 00:00 | 23:00 |

The Noise Control Policy sets max_decibel_limit at 90 dB. Record status: current.

Note: Curfew refers to the time by which all amplified sound must cease. Sound
checks and rehearsals must be completed at least 30 minutes before the curfew time.

6. FREQUENCY WEIGHTING AND AVERAGING
All measurements shall use A-weighting (dBA) unless otherwise specified by the
NEA or by the venue’s licence conditions. The Leq over 15 minutes shall be the
primary metric for compliance. In addition, the Lpeak (peak sound pressure level)
shall not exceed 120 dBA at any time, regardless of duration.

For events with multiple sound sources (e.g., multiple stages), each stage shall be
measured independently, and the combined effect shall be assessed by the Production
Manager. If the combined Leq is expected to exceed 90 dB, the sound engineers for
each stage shall coordinate to reduce output.

7. ROLES AND RESPONSIBILITIES
7.1 Production Manager
- Overall responsibility for compliance with this policy.
- Appoints a designated Noise Monitor for each event.
- Reviews logged data and signs off on the post-event noise report.

7.2 Noise Monitor
- Operates the SLM and records measurements.
- Reports any exceedance immediately to the Production Manager and the stage
  sound engineer.
- Maintains the measurement log in the format specified in Appendix A.

7.3 Sound Engineer (Head of Sound)
- Ensures system configuration (speaker placement, EQ, limiting) is set to avoid
  exceedances.
- Adjusts levels upon instruction from the Noise Monitor.
- Provides technical explanation for any exceedance.

8. CURFEW SCHEDULE AND AMPLIFIED SOUND CEASURE

8.1 General Curfew Time

The Noise Control Policy curfew_time is 22:30. Record status: current. This is the standard curfew time for all events under this policy, unless a later time is approved under the conditions in Section 8.3 below. Curfew time means the time by which all amplified sound must cease, including sound checks, rehearsals, and any audio output from stage monitors, PA systems, or broadcast speakers. This applies to both indoor and outdoor venues within the event site, including back-of-house areas where amplified sound may be audible to the public or nearby residential premises.

All event schedules shall be planned such that the final musical performance or programme item ends no later than 15 minutes before the curfew time. This buffer allows for encores, on-stage announcements, and the orderly fade-out of sound. The curfew time is not the same as the venue's operational closing time; the venue may remain open for audience egress, food and beverage sales, and non-amplified activities, subject to the venue's own licence conditions.

8.2 Curfew by Venue Type and Day

The following table sets out the curfew times applicable to different venue types. These are the curfew times, meaning amplified sound must cease by the stated time. Where the venue type is not listed, the curfew time shall be 22:30 unless otherwise approved.

Note: For Sundays and public holidays, the curfew time reverts to 22:30 for park/open field venues. This is to account for the following day being a working day for most residents.

8.3 Extensions and Exceptions

Requests for a later curfew time may be submitted to the Production Manager in writing at least 14 days before the event. The following criteria shall be considered:

- Distance to nearest residential premises (minimum 150 m for a 30-minute extension; minimum 300 m for a 60-minute extension)
- Historical noise complaint records for the venue
- Whether the event is a national or community event with a public interest justification
- Weather conditions (e.g., a delayed start due to an afternoon thunderstorm may justify a later end time, but not a later curfew)

Approved extensions shall be recorded in the event's Noise Management Plan and communicated to the Noise Monitor and sound engineers. Extensions are not automatically granted and must be confirmed in writing by the Production Manager.

8.4 Sound Checks and Rehearsals

Sound checks and rehearsals are subject to the same curfew time as the main event. All sound checks must be completed at least 30 minutes before the curfew time. This means that if the curfew is 22:30, all sound checks must be completed by 22:00.

During sound checks, the Noise Monitor shall take preliminary measurements and note any potential exceedance of the 90 dB limit. If the sound check indicates that the main performance is likely to exceed the limit, the Sound Engineer shall adjust the system configuration before the performance begins. No sound check may be conducted after the curfew time, even if the main event has not yet started.

9. ENFORCEMENT AND MONITORING PROCEDURES

9.1 Noise Monitor Duties During Event

The Noise Monitor shall:

- Take measurements at 15-minute intervals throughout the event, starting at least 30 minutes before the first performance and continuing until 15 minutes after the curfew time.
- Record the Leq, Lpeak, and the time of each measurement in the log sheet (Appendix A).
- Note the location of each measurement and any relevant conditions (e.g., wind direction, crowd noise, nearby construction).
- Immediately report any reading that exceeds 90 dB (Leq, 15-min) or 120 dBA (Lpeak) to the Production Manager and the stage Sound Engineer.

*Note: Rev 3.1 remains the last approved version for operational use until Rev 3.2 is formally endorsed. Any reference to "this policy" in the body below refers to the draft under review unless stated otherwise.*

---

**1. PURPOSE**

This policy establishes the framework for managing noise emissions from all Lumina Events activities, including but not limited to concerts, festivals, corporate functions, and community events held at venues operated or managed by Lumina Events Pte Ltd. The purpose is to ensure compliance with the National Environment Agency (NEA) regulations, to minimise disturbance to surrounding residents and businesses, and to maintain good community relations.

This policy applies to all Lumina Events staff, contractors, sub-contractors, volunteers, and artists performing at Lumina Events venues or events. It also applies to external parties who hire Lumina Events venues for their own events, and such parties shall be made aware of this policy as part of the venue hire agreement.

**2. DEFINITIONS**

For the purposes of this policy, the following terms shall have the meanings described below:

- **Ambient Noise:** The background noise level at a given location, measured in the absence of the event noise. This is typically measured during a quiet period, such as early afternoon, and is used as a baseline for assessing the impact of event noise.
- **Curfew Time:** The time by which all amplified sound, including sound checks and rehearsals, must cease. The standard curfew time is 22:30 hours, unless a written extension has been approved under Section 8.3.
- **Decibel (dB):** A unit of measurement for sound intensity. Unless otherwise specified, all decibel limits in this policy refer to A-weighted decibels (dBA) for Lpeak and Leq,15min measurements.
- **Intermittent Event:** An event or portion of an event that produces sound at irregular intervals, with periods of relative quiet between performances or announcements. Examples include multi-stage festivals where stages alternate, or events with scheduled breaks.
- **Leq,15min:** The equivalent continuous sound level measured over a 15-minute period. This is the primary metric used for assessing compliance with the 90 dB limit.
- **Lpeak:** The peak sound pressure level, measured instantaneously. This is used to assess the risk of hearing damage and sudden loud noises.
- **Noise Monitor:** A trained individual appointed by the Production Manager to carry out sound level measurements and report on compliance. The Noise Monitor shall be independent of the sound system provider.
- **Noise Management Plan (NMP):** A document prepared for each event, detailing the predicted sound levels, mitigation measures, monitoring arrangements, and contingency plans. The NMP shall be submitted to the relevant authorities as required.
- **Sound Engineer:** The individual responsible for the operation of the sound system during the event, including system configuration, mixing, and ensuring compliance with the sound level limits.
- **Venue Boundary:** The physical boundary of the event site, as indicated on the site plan attached to the NMP. For venues without a defined boundary, the boundary shall be the perimeter of the area under Lumina Events' control.

Crowd Management Plan – Annual Updates
Lumina Events Pte Ltd
Document Ref: CMP-2025-REV3
Version Control Owner: Operations & Safety Division

---

1.0 Purpose and Scope

This document consolidates the crowd management arrangements for Lumina Events Pte Ltd outdoor and mixed-venue events held within Singapore. It covers capacity planning, entry and exit operations, staffing requirements, and density control measures. The plan is reviewed annually and updated where site conditions, event formats, or regulatory feedback require revision.

This edition reflects the arrangements for the 2025 event calendar. Where a section has been revised since the previous annual update, the change is noted in the margin or in the revision summary at the end of the relevant section. Superseded figures from earlier editions are retained in the appendix for audit reference only and must not be used for operational planning.

2.0 Venue Capacity Determination

2.1 General Principle

The maximum capacity for any event site is determined by the lesser of the physical site capacity, the approved capacity under the Fire Safety (Events Venues) Order, and the operational capacity recommended by the Safety & Security Consultant. The maximum capacity figure is fixed for the current calendar year and is not adjusted on a per-event basis unless a formal variation is approved by the relevant authorities.

The Crowd Management Plan max_capacity is 50000 people. Record status: current. This figure is current for the 2025 edition and applies to the main festival grounds at Bayfront Green, including the open field area, the promenade extensions, and the designated viewing zones. The figure excludes performers, crew, vendors, and accredited media personnel, who are accounted for separately under the staffing and production headcount.

2.2 Capacity Calculation Basis

The site is divided into zones for the purpose of capacity calculation and crowd density monitoring. Each zone has its own holding capacity, which when summed, equals the overall maximum capacity. The zoning reflects the physical layout, the location of entry and exit points, and the internal circulation routes.

Table 2.1: Zone Capacity Breakdown (2025 Edition)

| Zone | Area (sqm) | Density Standard (persons/sqm) | Holding Capacity |
|------|------------|-------------------------------|------------------|
| A – Main Field | 18,500 | 1.2 (standing, concert) | 22,200 |
| B – Promenade East | 6,200 | 1.0 (mixed circulation) | 6,200 |
| C – Promenade West | 5,800 | 1.0 (mixed circulation) | 5,800 |
| D – Viewing Decks | 2,400 | 0.8 (seated/standing mix) | 1,920 |
| E – Food & Retail Village | 4,100 | 1.5 (queuing and movement) | 6,150 |
| F – Chill-out Zone | 3,200 | 0.7 (low-density lounging) | 2,240 |
| G – Entry/Exit Buffer | 2,800 | 2.0 (transit only, not holding) | 5,600 (transit) |
| Total | 43,000 | – | 50,000 (approx.) |

The sum of the holding capacities for Zones A–F is 44,510. The remaining capacity of 5,490 is allocated to the transit buffer (Zone G) and to the internal walkways that connect the zones. The transit buffer is not intended for prolonged occupation; it exists to absorb the surge of people entering or exiting during peak periods. If the transit buffer becomes congested for more than 10 minutes, entry is paused at the affected gates.

2.3 Density Monitoring

Zone density is monitored using a combination of manual headcounts at the gates, CCTV analytics at key pinch points, and steward patrols with handheld counters. The density standard for each zone is set out in Table 2.1 above. The following thresholds trigger action:

- 80% of zone holding capacity: Stewards at the zone entry points begin to hold back incoming attendees, and the zone controller is notified.
- 90% of zone holding capacity: Zone entry is closed to all new attendees. Re-routing messages are broadcast over the PA system and on the digital signage.
- 100% of zone holding capacity: The zone is declared full. Attendees are directed to alternative zones or to the transit buffer. No further entry is permitted until the density drops below 85%.

### Revision Log (Continuation)

### 4. Crowd Density Thresholds and Response Protocols

#### 4.1 Density Threshold Standard

The crowd density threshold for all event zones is **4 people per square meter**. This is the maximum design density for short-duration (≤ 15 minutes) peak loads, as certified by CrowdSafe Technologies in their 2025 system calibration report. It applies to all zones and all event configurations, unless a lower zone-specific standard is set out in Table 2.1.

**Table 4.1: Density Threshold Triggers**

#### 4.2 Monitoring and Reporting

Density is monitored centrally at the Crowd Safety Cell (CSC), located in the North Command Post (NCP). The CSC operates from 10:00 to 24:00 on event days, with a skeleton team from 08:00 (for load-in checks). Key monitoring tools:

- **CCTV Analytics:** 42 cameras across 11 zones, with automated people-counting software. Calibration is checked each morning against manual counts at 3 fixed reference points.
- **Handheld Counters:** Stewards at zone entry/exit points conduct 10-minute manual counts during peak periods (17:00–21:00).
- **Steward Patrols:** Roving stewards visually assess density every 15 minutes, reporting via radio code "Density Check [Zone] [Level]".

The Crowd Management Plan crowd_density_threshold is 4 people per square meter. Record status: current.

**Reporting Cadence:**

- **Every 30 minutes** during normal operations (written log).
- **Every 10 minutes** when any zone is at ≥ 80% of the density threshold.
- **Continuous** (radio update every 2 minutes) when any zone is at ≥ 90%.

All density readings are logged in the CSC Daily Log (Form CSC-7). The log is reviewed at the end of each event day by the Event Director and the Safety & Security Lead.

#### 4.3 Response Protocols

The following protocols are activated based on the density levels in Table 4.1. These are in addition to the zone-specific capacity actions in Section 2.3.

**Protocol 1 – Density Watch (≥ 3.0 persons/sqm)**

- CSC announces "Density Watch" over the command radio channel (Ch 1).
- Zone Controllers confirm receipt and identify the affected zone(s).
- Gate stewards begin holding entry at the affected zone(s) for 30-second intervals.
- Additional stewards are dispatched from the reserve pool (minimum 4 per affected zone).
- The Event Director is informed verbally, but no written report is required unless the level persists for > 30 minutes.

**Protocol 2 – Zone Hold (≥ 3.2 persons/sqm)**

**Protocol 3 – Zone Closure (≥ 3.6 persons/sqm)**

- Zone entry is closed to all new attendees.
- PA and digital signage broadcast re-routing messages (pre-recorded message "Route B" or "Route C", depending on the zone).
- Exit gates are widened where possible (barriers moved by stewards).
- The Event Director is formally notified via radio and a written SMS alert.
- SCDF Liaison (Kelvin Chua) is informed if the closure lasts > 15 minutes.

**Protocol 4 – Full Stop (≥ 4.0 persons/sqm)**

**Post-Incident Requirements:**

- A written Incident Report (Form IR-2) must be submitted within 2 hours of any Protocol 3 or 4 activation.
- The report must include: time of activation, measured density readings, duration, actions taken, and any attendee feedback or incidents.
- The Safety & Security Lead reviews the report and recommends any adjustments to the plan.

## 5. Communication Protocols

### 5.1 Command Structure and Radio Channels

All crowd management communications shall follow the tiered command structure below. The structure applies to all Lumina Events productions, including the annual Marina Bay Lights Festival and the Sentosa Music Weekend.

| Tier | Role | Radio Channel | Call Sign Prefix |
|------|------|---------------|------------------|
| 1 | Event Director | Ch 1 (Command) | ED |
| 2 | Safety & Security Lead | Ch 1 (Command) | SSL |
| 3 | Crowd Safety Controller (CSC) | Ch 1 (Command) | CSC |
| 4 | Zone Controllers (per zone) | Ch 2 (Operations) | ZC-[Zone] |
| 5 | Gate Stewards / Marshals | Ch 3 (Tactical) | GS-[Number] |
| 6 | First Aid / Medical Team | Ch 4 (Medical) | MED |
| 7 | SCDF Liaison | Ch 1 (Command) | SCDF |

**Radio Etiquette:**

- All radio transmissions shall begin with the call sign of the recipient followed by the call sign of the sender. Example: "ZC-East, this is CSC, over."
- Use plain English. Avoid jargon or slang. Do not use "lah" or other Singlish particles on the radio channel, as these can cause confusion during high-stress situations.
- Acknowledge all instructions with "Copy" or "Received." If an instruction is unclear, respond with "Say again" or "Blur, please repeat."
- Non-urgent traffic (e.g., shift change updates) shall use Ch 2. Urgent traffic (e.g., density threshold breaches) shall use Ch 1.
- All radio batteries shall be checked at the start of each shift. Spare batteries are held at the CSC desk and at each Zone Controller post.

### 5.2 Communication During Incidents

During any activation of Protocol 1 through 4 (see Section 4.3), the following communication steps shall apply in addition to the response protocols:

1. The CSC shall broadcast a **situational update** on Ch 1 every 5 minutes until the protocol is stood down.
2. Zone Controllers shall provide a **verbal status report** every 10 minutes, or more frequently if directed by the CSC.
3. The Safety & Security Lead shall maintain a **written timeline** of all radio communications related to the incident. This timeline shall be attached to the Incident Report (Form IR-2) if one is required.
4. The Event Director shall be the only person authorised to communicate with external agencies (SCDF, Singapore Police Force, Land Transport Authority) regarding the incident. The SCDF Liaison (Kelvin Chua) may relay operational details but shall not make public statements.
5. For Protocol 3 or 4 activations, the Event Director shall send an SMS alert to the following:
   - SCDF Operations Centre (via Liaison)
   - Lumina Events Head of Security (Ms. Priya Nair)
   - Lumina Events Legal & Compliance (Mr. Daniel Koh)

**Public Communication:**

- PA announcements shall be made in English, Mandarin, and Malay. A pre-recorded Tamil version is available for download from the CSC desk if the event demographic requires it.
- Digital signage shall display messages in the same four languages where screen space permits. On smaller screens, English and Mandarin shall take priority.
- All PA scripts must be approved by the Event Director before the event day. Approved scripts are stored at the CSC desk in the "PA Scripts" binder.
- Do not announce density levels to the public. Use operational language such as "the area is currently full" or "please use the alternate route."
